A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title, authors, and central contributions. All 23 pages of each version, including appendices A–H, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on synthetic moons, pixel-swapped MNIST, and binary MNIST/CIFAR100 tasks, alongside numerical bound comparisons in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds representation-size analyses, bound diagnostics, and a MNIST label-shuffle experiment.

M1.justification: The PBH, SCH−, SCH+, and PB SCH architectures, training objectives, sampling procedures, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Corrected bound formulas and relocated architecture diagrams do not establish a change to the underlying learning procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix H and Table 8 add MNIST tasks with randomly permuted labels, a distinct scenario from the retained pixel permutations and binary class comparisons. Existing dataset coverage remains. The new experiment is described as multiclass in the prose but called binary in Table 8's caption.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and v2 Table 4/v3 Table 5. The new label-shuffle comparison reuses the six literature comparators already evaluated on binary tasks. MotherNet is discussed as future inspiration, not evaluated as a new baseline.

E3.justification: The added label-shuffle experiment uses 30 training tasks of 1,000 examples and 10 test tasks of 100 examples. Figure 7 adds a joint compression/message-size sweep, including compression size 12 beyond the previously listed grid. Reported settings for the original experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Figure 7 tests compression/message-size trade-offs, Table 4 compares baseline prior–posterior KL values, and Figure 9 with Tables 6–7 decomposes bound contributions. Appendix H also adds the label-shuffle failure analysis. The earlier moons illustrations and theoretical bound comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals across test tasks. v3 extends this existing practice to additional results without introducing a different uncertainty estimator, significance test, or new seed/repeated-training-run disclosure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and v2 Table 4/v3 Table 5 retain identical numerical results. However, v3 adds substantial sensitivity and bound-component results and an important failure case: Table 8 reports PB SCH label-shuffle error 0.792 ± 0.070 and bound 0.997 ± 0.005, versus Amit and Meir's 0.023 ± 0.062 and 0.542 ± 0.034 in that experiment.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 correct the compression-bound empirical-loss argument from the full task sample to its compression-set complement. Corollary C.3 is correctly placed under Theorem B.2 instead of B.1, and Appendix B revises the moment-generating-function derivation. The central theorem family is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions are unchanged. The conclusion limits its criticism to 'many' PAC-Bayes approaches and explicitly conditions applicability to very large models on task-varying parameters admitting a compact representation, such as a LoRA adapter.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of compression/message-size trade-offs and the contributions controlling bound tightness. Appendix H reports severe meta-training overfitting on label-shuffled tasks and hypothesizes insufficient DeepSet expressiveness. These additions materially expand the documented mechanisms and failure conditions beyond v2's existing noisy-MNIST discussion.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix H newly provide a DeepRM code-repository address and state that experimental code is available. Existing architecture grids, optimizer, initialization, hardware, and stopping-rule descriptions are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds two Lotfi et al. 2024 papers on language-model bounds and Mueller et al.'s MotherNet, while removing Lotfi et al. 2022 and several older compression references. These are limited contextual changes. The Bazinet and Attias year/venue updates refer to retained works rather than new citations.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable. Local revisions add SVM and decision-stump examples, clarify the scope of downstream-predictor guarantees, refine proof explanations and the conclusion, add acknowledgements, and abbreviate bibliographic entries. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the displays: PAC-Bayes and hybrid architecture diagrams move from Appendix G into Section 3, the duplicate sample-compression diagram disappears, and old Figures 5–6 become Figure 8's paired panels. New sensitivity and decomposition figures and Tables 4, 6–8 expand and rearrange the main-text and appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity and bound-decomposition analyses make the retained methods easier to assess, while the reported label-shuffle failure and qualified large-model claim better document applicability limits. Formula corrections and code-access information also help. These provide a limited net improvement; the new experiment's conflicting multiclass/binary descriptions leave some reporting ambiguity.
